heroIntro: Purchasing an apartment in Dhaka, Chattogram, or other urban hubs represents one of the most substantial financial investments an individual or expatriate family will ever undertake. Beyond agreed builder instalment schedules, prospective buyers must account for mandatory statutory registration expenses, including Stamp Duty, Sub-Registry Fees, Local Government Taxes, Advance Income Tax (AIT), and National Board of Revenue (NBR) developer VAT. Without formal registration under the Registration Act 1908 and the Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010, an allotment letter or developer agreement confers no proprietary title. This comprehensive legal guide by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Advocate and land law practitioner in Uttara and the Dhaka Judge Court, delivers an authoritative fee calculation matrix, document checklist, and developer dispute remedies.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Overview: Flat Registration Cost Breakdown in Bangladesh (2026)
quickAnswer.heading: Quick Overview: Flat Registration Cost Breakdown in Bangladesh (2026)
quickAnswer.text: In 2026, total apartment registration costs in Bangladesh typically range from 7.5% to 11% of deed valuation depending on urban jurisdiction and developer VAT tier. Core statutory components include: (1) Registration Fee at 1% of deed valuation under the Registration Act 1908; (2) Stamp Duty at 1.5% under the Stamp Act 1899; (3) Local Government Tax at 3% in City Corporation areas (Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Gazipur) or 2% in Municipalities (Pourashavas); (4) Advance Income Tax (AIT / Source Tax) under the Income Tax Act 2023, assessed either per square meter (typically 1,000 to 2,000 BDT/sqm in prime commercial zones) or 2% to 4% on deed valuation; and (5) NBR Developer VAT of 2% for flats up to 1,600 sq ft or 4.5% for flats exceeding 1,600 sq ft. Re-sale flats between individual citizens are completely exempt from developer VAT.

sections.title: 1. Legal Framework: Registration Act 1908 & Real Estate Act 2010
sections.content:
In Bangladesh, apartment ownership is not merely a commercial handover of keys; it is a formal conveyance of proportionate undivided and indivisible land share coupled with physical apartment space. Under Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908 and Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882, any transfer of immovable property exceeding 100 BDT in value must be effected through a registered instrument. An allotment paper, money receipt, or unregistered builder booking agreement confers zero legal title in the eyes of a civil court.

The relationship between buyers and developers is regulated by the Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010 (Act No. XX of 2010). This legislation prohibits developers from selling apartments without prior project approval from development authorities (such as RAJUK, CDA, KDA, or RDA), mandates registration of developer power of attorney, and penalizes structural deviations or delivery defaults. When executing the final Saf-Kabala (Sale Deed), both the landowner and the developer holding a registered Power of Attorney must join as executants to ensure valid passage of title.

Understanding statutory expenses prevents unexpected financial strain during the final registration phase. For complex conveyancing, cross-checking chain deeds and vetting developer powers with a land lawyer in Bangladesh protects buyers from protracted title litigation.

sections.title: 2. Statutory Fee Schedule: Stamp Duty, Registration & Local Taxes
sections.content:
Statutory fees are computed either on the declared purchase price in the deed or the official government-notified minimum Mouza value (determined periodically by the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs), whichever amount is higher. Sub-Registrars strictly reject undervalued deed submissions.

The core statutory schedule across various geographic jurisdictions in Bangladesh is summarized below:

Statutory Cost HeadCity Corporation (DNCC, DSCC, CCC)Municipality (Pourashava)Union Parishad / Rural
Registration Fee1.0% of Deed Valuation1.0% of Deed Valuation1.0% of Deed Valuation
Stamp Duty1.5% of Deed Valuation1.5% of Deed Valuation1.5% of Deed Valuation
Local Government Tax3.0% (City Corporation)2.0% (Pourashava)1.0% (Union Parishad)
Affidavit Fee300 BDT Stamp300 BDT Stamp300 BDT Stamp
Sub-Registry N-Fee & E-FeeBDT 240 + Page Copying FeeBDT 240 + Page Copying FeeBDT 240 + Page Copying Fee

All fees are deposited directly into designated treasury accounts at Sonali Bank branches using automated e-Chalan codes. Cash payments directly to Sub-Registry personnel are prohibited under Directorate of Registration anti-corruption circulars.

sections.title: 3. Advance Income Tax (AIT) & NBR Developer VAT Rules (2026)
sections.content:
In addition to standard registration fees, apartment transactions involve direct and indirect taxes administered under the Income Tax Act 2023 and the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

Advance Income Tax (AIT / Source Tax): Under Section 125 of the Income Tax Act 2023, source tax must be collected by the registering officer prior to registration. In commercial areas and prime residential sectors of Dhaka (such as Gulshan, Banani, Motijheel, Dhanmondi, Uttara, and Bashundhara), AIT for apartments is levied on a fixed square-meter basis, ranging from 1,000 BDT to 2,000 BDT per square meter. In other residential areas, it is calculated as a percentage (typically 2% to 4%) of deed valuation. By standard legal convention, AIT is the statutory liability of the seller or developer, representing advance tax on business turnover or capital gains.

Developer VAT (NBR Statutory Regulatory Orders): When purchasing directly from a commercial builder or REHAB-affiliated developer, VAT is payable on the building construction value:

  • Apartments up to 1,600 Square Feet: 2.0% VAT on deed valuation.
  • Apartments exceeding 1,600 Square Feet: 4.5% VAT on deed valuation.
  • Commercial Space & Office Suites: 15.0% standard VAT.
  • Private Re-sale Flats (Citizen to Citizen): 0% VAT. Re-sale transactions between individuals do not attract developer VAT because no commercial development service is rendered.

sections.title: 5. Pre-Purchase Legal Checklist: Title Deeds, CS/RS/BS & AC Land Mutation
sections.content:
Careful legal due diligence prior to signing any contract or advancing earnest money is vital. A real estate advocate checks a 30-year unbroken chain of title documents before approving an apartment purchase:

  1. Mother Title Deed (Mool Dalil): Verify original ownership deeds of the underlying land. If acquired through inheritance, verify partition deeds (Bonton-nama) or civil court partition decrees.
  2. Record of Rights (Khatian Porcha): Examine Cadastral Survey (CS), State Acquisition (SA), Revisional Survey (RS), and Dhaka City Jarip (BS) records. Ensure the landowner's name matches the latest recorded Khatian.
  3. AC Land E-Namjari Mutation: Confirm that the landowner or developer has completed digital mutation with the relevant Upazila / Circle AC Land office and holds a formal DCR (Duplicate Carbon Receipt) and mutation Khatian.
  4. Land Development Tax (Dakhila): Inspect updated online land development tax receipts for the current Bengali calendar fiscal year.
  5. Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC): Conduct an official search at the Sub-Registry Office for the past 12 to 30 years to confirm that the underlying land is free from mortgages, bank hypothecations, or pending civil litigation.

Review our checklist on buying land in Bangladesh from abroad for detailed remote vetting protocols.

sections.title: 6. Building Plan Vetting: RAJUK / CDA Layout Approval & Occupancy Certificate
sections.content:
A registered land title is insufficient if the physical building violates urban planning and structural safety laws. In Dhaka, development is supervised by the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK); in Chattogram, by the Chattogram Development Authority (CDA); and in other cities by corresponding regional development bodies.

Buyers must verify the following statutory approvals:

  • Special Project Approval & Land Use Clearance: Confirmation that the plot is designated for residential use under the Master Plan.
  • Approved Building Plan (Sthapotik Noksha): Inspect the official architecturally sanctioned plan bearing the official seal and file reference number of RAJUK or CDA. Cross-check approved floor heights, setbacks, car parking allocations, and Far (Floor Area Ratio) limits.
  • Unauthorized Floor Inspection: If the approved plan sanctions 8 stories but the developer has constructed 10 stories, purchasing an apartment on the 9th or 10th floor is illegal. The Sub-Registrar cannot legally register an unauthorized floor, and RAJUK retains powers of demolition.
  • Occupancy Certificate: Under the Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) and RAJUK rules, developers must obtain an Occupancy Certificate confirming that construction strictly matches approved plans before utility connections and residential occupancy are lawful.

sections.title: 7. Step-by-Step Flat Deed Execution & Sub-Registry Procedure
sections.content:
The legal process of formal conveyance at the Sub-Registry Office follows structured procedural stages:

  1. Drafting the Deed of Sale: The deed must accurately detail the proportionate land share, apartment number, floor level, super built-up area, common facility allocations, and car park demarcations.
  2. Chalan Generation and Fee Payment: Registration fees, stamp duty, local government taxes, and AIT are deposited through treasury chalans at Sonali Bank.
  3. Physical or Biometric Attendance: The buyer and the developer's authorized representative appear before the Sub-Registrar. Both parties submit biometric fingerprint verification matched against the Election Commission NID database.
  4. Execution & Registration Endorsement: The Sub-Registrar examines identity credentials, confirms payment chalans, and signs the registration order.
  5. Issuance of Form-52 Receipt: The buyer receives an official Form-52 token receipt. The original registered volume deed is released upon final volume binding, typically within several months.
  6. Individual Post-Purchase Mutation: Following registration, the buyer must immediately apply for an individual AC Land e-Namjari mutation in their own name and separate holding tax registration with the City Corporation.

sections.title: 8. Legal Remedies Against Developer Delay, Fraud, or Non-Registration
sections.content:
When a developer delays handover, constructs substandard facilities, or refuses to execute registration, buyers possess actionable statutory remedies under Bangladeshi law:

  • Statutory Compensation under Real Estate Act 2010: Under Section 15 of Act No. XX of 2010, if a developer fails to deliver possession within the agreed contractual period, they must pay compensation interest at 15% per annum on the total amount paid by the purchaser for the delay period.
  • Formal Legal Notice: The buyer must dispatch a formal Legal Notice drafted by a Supreme Court advocate demanding completion, registration, and compensation within 30 to 60 days.
  • REHAB Dispute Resolution: If the developer is a registered member of the Real Estate & Housing Association of Bangladesh (REHAB), complaints can be lodged with the REHAB Mediation and Arbitration Cell.
  • Suit for Specific Performance of Contract: Under the Specific Relief Act 1877, the buyer can institute a suit before the Joint District Judge to legally compel the developer and landowner to execute the registered deed. Read our detailed analysis on breach of contract damages and specific performance in Bangladesh.
  • Criminal Complaint for Fraud and Embezzlement: If a developer sells the same flat to multiple buyers or mortgages the property to a bank without authorization, criminal proceedings under Sections 406 and 420 of the Penal Code 1860 can be initiated before a Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court.

sections.title: 9. Guidelines for NRBs & Expatriates Buying Flats in Bangladesh
sections.content:
Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) living in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and the Middle East represent a major segment of apartment buyers in Dhaka. However, managing transactions from abroad creates distinctive legal risks.

NRBs should adhere to these established safeguards:

  • Channel All Funds via Inward Banking Remittance: Always transfer purchase instalments through formal banking channels into a Non-Resident Foreign Currency Deposit (NFCD) or Non-Resident Investor's Taka Account (NITA). Official banking remittance certificates shield the buyer from National Board of Revenue scrutiny and enable legitimate fund repatriation if the property is later liquidated.
  • Execution of Special Power of Attorney: If the expatriate buyer cannot travel to Bangladesh for registration, they can execute a Special Power of Attorney appointing a trusted family member or advocate. The document must be executed and attested before the consular officer at the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission in their host country, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) in Dhaka, and stamped by the Collector of Stamps under the Power of Attorney Act 2012. Review our guide on power of attorney property transfer in Bangladesh.
  • Independent Chamber Vetting: Never rely on developer-provided lawyers. Retain independent legal counsel to verify title authenticity, RAJUK approvals, and encumbrance records directly at official land registries. Visit our NRB legal help service page for overseas legal representation.

sections.title: 10. Illustrative Scenario: Resolving Delayed Registration and Title Clearance
sections.content:
Illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed): An expatriate physician residing in London purchased a 1,650 square-foot apartment in Uttara Sector 11, Dhaka, paying 90% of the agreed 1.2 Crore BDT price over three years. Although physical handover occurred in late 2024, the developer repeatedly postponed deed registration, citing unresolved disputes with the original landowner over proportionate floor allocations.

Facing escalating uncertainty and unable to obtain an individual utility connection or mortgage, the overseas buyer retained Advocate Md. Shah Alam's chamber. Our legal intervention unfolded methodically:

  1. Retrieved certified records from the Sub-Registry Office and discovered that while the landowner had granted a registered Power of Attorney, the developer had failed to obtain an amended sanction from RAJUK for minor terrace adjustments.
  2. Issued a statutory 30-day Legal Notice under the Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010 to both the developer and the landowner, establishing their joint legal liability to convey title and claiming 15% statutory delay compensation.
  3. Convened a structured tripartite negotiation at our Uttara legal chamber between the developer's managing director and the landowner's legal representative.
  4. Drafted a tripartite Supplementary Conveyance Deed clarifying common space demarcations and ensuring all Sonali Bank treasury e-chalans for Stamp Duty, Local Government Tax, and Developer VAT were correctly apportioned.
  5. Supervised the final registration of the Saf-Kabala deed before the Sub-Registrar through an embassy-authenticated Special Power of Attorney, successfully securing the Form-52 receipt and subsequently completing the buyer's AC Land e-Namjari mutation without litigation.

faqs.question: What is the total flat registration cost percentage in Dhaka in 2026?
faqs.answer: In Dhaka City Corporation areas (DNCC and DSCC), total registration expenses generally range between 7.5% and 10.5% of deed valuation. This includes 1.0% Registration Fee, 1.5% Stamp Duty, 3.0% Local Government Tax, 2.0% to 4.5% Developer VAT (depending on square footage), and miscellaneous drafting/e-chalan charges.

faqs.question: Who is legally responsible for paying the developer VAT and Advance Income Tax (AIT)?
faqs.answer: By law, Advance Income Tax (AIT / Source Tax) is the legal liability of the seller or developer as advance business income tax. Developer VAT is assessed on the consumer by the NBR and is paid by the purchaser to the developer for deposit into the government exchequer. Private re-sale flats between individuals are entirely exempt from developer VAT.

faqs.question: Can a flat be registered without an individual AC Land e-Namjari mutation?
faqs.answer: For initial deed registration, the Sub-Registrar requires the parent land mutation (e-Namjari) in the name of the developer or landowner along with updated land tax (Dakhila). Once the flat is registered, the buyer must immediately submit an individual e-Namjari application on land.gov.bd to record their proportionate undivided land share.

faqs.question: What happens if a real estate developer delays handover or deed registration?
faqs.answer: Under Section 15 of the Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010, the developer is legally bound to compensate the buyer with 15% annual interest on all monies paid during the delay period. The purchaser can issue a formal Legal Notice and file a suit for Specific Performance of Contract in civil court.

faqs.question: How can overseas expatriates (NRBs) register an apartment without travelling to Dhaka?
faqs.answer: An expatriate can execute a Special Power of Attorney appointing a local family member or advocate. The document must be executed before a consular officer at the Bangladesh Embassy abroad, attested by MoFA in Dhaka, and validated by the Collector of Stamps before submission to the Sub-Registry Office.

faqs.question: Is an unregistered allotment letter or sale agreement legally enforceable?
faqs.answer: An unregistered allotment letter does not create proprietary title under Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908. It functions solely as evidence of a personal contract. To establish complete ownership enforceable against third parties, a registered Saf-Kabala (Sale Deed) is legally mandatory.

faqs.question: What is the difference between carpet area, super built-up area, and deed measurement?
faqs.answer: Carpet area represents actual usable indoor floor space within interior walls. Built-up area includes outer walls and balconies. Super built-up area adds a proportionate share of common spaces such as lobbies, stairs, and generator rooms. The deed specifies both the apartment super built-up area and the proportionate undivided land share.

faqs.question: What legal documents must a buyer collect from the developer after registration?
faqs.answer: Following registration, the buyer must collect: (1) Form-52 registration receipt and subsequent original certified registered Saf-Kabala deed; (2) Certified copies of the parent title deed and registered Power of Attorney; (3) Approved RAJUK/CDA architectural plans and Occupancy Certificate; and (4) Updated land development tax Dakhila.
